report.case_overview: Sara Hassan, 41‑year‑old female with well‑controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertension, presents for routine cleaning and examination. She has a severe penicillin allergy and mild latex sensitivity. Dental chart shows a carious lesion on tooth 27, an intact amalgam restoration on tooth 36 placed 2024‑06‑10, and a recent extraction of tooth 47 (2023‑08‑15). She reports cold sensitivity on the lower right side.

evidence_summary: Cold sensitivity may indicate reversible or irreversible pulpitis; pulp testing and radiographic assessment are required (evidence [3],[5])
Penicillin allergy requires alternative antibiotic prophylaxis if indicated (evidence [1])
Latex allergy mandates use of latex‑free gloves and materials (clinical best practice)
Diabetes, even when controlled, can affect wound healing; monitor post‑operative healing (general medical consideration)
Antihypertensive Lisinopril does not usually require alteration for dental procedures, but blood pressure should be checked (evidence [4])
Bisphosphonate or anticoagulant use increases surgical risk; none reported for this patient (evidence [1],[4])
medication_considerations: Metformin and Lisinopril have no known interaction; continue as prescribed
Avoid penicillin‑type antibiotics; consider clindamycin if prophylaxis is needed
ACE inhibitors may potentiate hypotensive response to epinephrine; use minimal epinephrine concentration and monitor blood pressure
Assess renal function before prescribing NSAIDs or adjusting Metformin dose
Monitor blood glucose peri‑operatively due to diabetes

report.draft_conclusion: The patient presents for routine care but reports cold sensitivity in the lower right quadrant, warranting pulp vitality testing and periapical radiographs of teeth 27, 36, and 46. The carious lesion on tooth 27 should be restored, preferably with composite resin using latex‑free isolation; a glass ionomer may be considered if composite is unavailable. The existing amalgam on tooth 36 appears intact, but its role in the sensitivity should be evaluated. No prophylactic antibiotics are indicated unless invasive work is planned; if needed, clindamycin is a suitable alternative to penicillin. Use latex‑free gloves and instruments, and limit epinephrine concentration due to ACE‑inhibitor therapy. Verify current HbA1c, blood pressure, and renal function before proceeding, and obtain full periodontal charting to guide maintenance intervals. All decisions should be confirmed by the treating dentist.
